title: Two lists, two unanswered changes
summary: Compare a home dose with a discharge dose and a stopped medicine. The source does not explain the differences.

dossier.caregiver_concerns: The old Lisinopril bottle is still on the kitchen table. Which list should we ask the discharge team to confirm?

documents.text:
Before admission, taking Lisinopril 10 mg by mouth QD.
Before admission, taking Aspirin 81 mg by mouth QD.

At discharge, take Lisinopril 5 mg by mouth BID.
At discharge, stop Aspirin 81 mg by mouth QD.

title: A change with an explicit explanation
summary: An addendum explicitly records an intentional dose change. A difference is not automatically an error.

dossier.caregiver_concerns: We understand there was a planned change to Lisinopril but want the team to explain the two lists together.

documents.text: Before admission, taking Lisinopril 10 mg by mouth QD.
At discharge, take Lisinopril 5 mg by mouth BID.
Intentional change: Lisinopril 5 mg by mouth BID replaces home Lisinopril 10 mg by mouth QD.

title: A taper that cannot become one dose
summary: Keep both dose phases, their sequence, their day anchor and the final stop instruction intact.

dossier.caregiver_concerns: The calendar starts on the day we arrive home. Does that match the Prednisone taper day anchor?

documents.text: Taper Prednisone: 20 mg by mouth QD on days 1-3; then 10 mg by mouth QD on days 4-6; then stop.
The discharge date is the recorded day anchor. The caregiver asks the team to confirm the calendar before using it.

title: Hold conditions and restart authority
summary: Preserve a comparator, the AND connector and the explicit requirement for team confirmation. A new lab value does not authorize restart.

dossier.caregiver_concerns: If the pressure improves but dizziness remains, who confirms whether Lisinopril can restart?

documents.text:
At discharge, take Lisinopril 5 mg by mouth QD.
Hold Lisinopril while systolic blood pressure < 100 mmHg AND dizziness = present; restart only after the discharge team confirms.
Systolic blood pressure recorded at 104 mmHg. This observation does not contain a restart order.

title: An old bottle and a different release form
summary: Use caregiver context to ask about identity and formulation. Name similarity does not establish interchangeability.

dossier.caregiver_concerns: The old bottle says Lopressor and the new list says Metoprolol succinate ER. Are the brand and release form the same?

documents.text: Before admission, taking Lopressor 25 mg by mouth BID.
At discharge, take Metoprolol succinate ER 50 mg by mouth QD.

title: A pending result without an owner
summary: Connect the pending result and caregiver question to a named owner and follow-up clarification. Do not invent the result or a medicine change.

dossier.caregiver_concerns: The potassium result is still pending. We do not know who will call us or whether a follow-up appointment exists.

documents.text:
At discharge, take Furosemide 20 mg by mouth QD.
Pending test: potassium; owner: not assigned; follow-up: within 2 days.
At discharge, take Warfarin 2.5 mg by mouth QHS.

The caregiver has the hospital switchboard number but no named follow-up contact.
The caregiver reports taking Ibuprofen 200 mg by mouth TID from an old bottle and asks the pharmacist to check it.
